role_archetypes.archetype: name: scout purpose: fast, shallow extraction; no synthesis, no judgment typical_model: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 typical_effort: low typical_tools: [Read, Grep, Glob] permission_mode: default isolation: single-subagent when_to_use: | You need a fast map of a codebase, a list of files matching a pattern, or verbatim excerpts from one or more sources. The role reports raw findings — it does not synthesize or evaluate them. Use when completeness and speed outweigh deliberation. when_NOT_to_use: | The task requires comparing findings, making recommendations, judging quality, or synthesizing across sources. Those belong to analyst, planner, or critic roles. example_prompt_shape: | "Find all files matching in . For each file, return the line number and full text of every match. Do not synthesize or summarize — return raw findings with file paths."

name: analyst purpose: synthesis from scout outputs or structured sources; produces written reports typical_model: claude-sonnet-4-6 typical_effort: medium typical_tools: [Read, Grep, Glob, Write] permission_mode: default isolation: single-subagent when_to_use: | You have raw scout findings that need cross-source synthesis, or structured inputs that need reasoning and report generation. Analyst roles read widely and write summary output; they do not modify production code. when_NOT_to_use: | Adversarial review (use critic). Long-horizon architecture decisions (use architect). Simple extraction where Haiku at low effort suffices (use scout to keep cost down). example_prompt_shape: | "Given these scout findings: , synthesize a summary that identifies . Write the output to . Cite the specific files that support each claim."

name: planner purpose: draft plans and design documents without executing any code changes typical_model: claude-sonnet-4-6 typical_effort: medium typical_tools: [Read, Grep, Glob] permission_mode: plan isolation: single-subagent when_to_use: | You want structured, deliberate planning before any code changes. Plan mode keeps the subagent in a propose-only state — it cannot call Write, Edit, or Bash. Use when the desired output is a plan document, not a code change. when_NOT_to_use: | Implementation tasks (analyst or architect). Roles that must write files as part of their output (plan mode blocks Write). Any task where the subagent must produce code or modify files. example_prompt_shape: | "Review the existing architecture in and draft an implementation plan for . Do not make any changes — produce only a plan document describing the approach, risks, and sequencing."

name: critic purpose: adversarial review; surfaces failure modes, contradictions, and gaps; does NOT mutate code typical_model: claude-opus-4-7 typical_effort: xhigh typical_tools: [Read, Grep, Glob] permission_mode: default isolation: single-subagent effort_rationale: | xhigh is the recommended starting point for Opus 4.7 coding and agentic work (official-effort.md, verified 2026-04-28). Adversarial review is judgment-heavy — the critic must hold full context to find non-obvious failure paths. xhigh is Opus 4.7 only; use high on Opus 4.6 or Sonnet 4.6 when cost requires. when_to_use: | You want an independent adversarial perspective on a design, plan, or implementation. Critic roles read only — they never write to production code. Use after analyst or architect roles produce a draft. when_NOT_to_use: | Simple correctness checks where Sonnet medium suffices. Tasks that require producing output documents (no write tools present). When you want constructive suggestions rather than adversarial challenge (use analyst). example_prompt_shape: | "Review . Find failure modes, missing edge cases, and false assumptions. Produce a prioritized list of objections with specific citations (file + line). Do not suggest fixes — identify gaps only."

name: architect purpose: cross-system design; produces architecture documents and code scaffolds typical_model: claude-opus-4-7 typical_effort: xhigh typical_tools: [Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit] permission_mode: default isolation: single-subagent effort_rationale: | xhigh is the explicitly recommended starting point for Opus 4.7 coding and agentic work (official-effort.md, verified 2026-04-28). Bump to max only if evals on the specific workload show measurable headroom over xhigh — expect significant cost increase for marginal quality gain otherwise. when_to_use: | Cross-system design requiring wide codebase reads and production of both design documents and code scaffolds. Higher blast radius than analyst or critic — this role can write and edit files. when_NOT_to_use: | Adversarial review (use critic — no write tools). Simple synthesis (use analyst at lower cost). Propose-only roles (use planner with plan mode). example_prompt_shape: | "Analyze the architecture of . Design the integration for : produce an architecture document at and scaffold the key files with stubs. Explain each decision."

name: lead purpose: team coordinator; routes work to teammates via SendMessage and TaskCreate typical_model: claude-sonnet-4-6 typical_effort: medium typical_tools: [Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Task, SendMessage] permission_mode: default isolation: team-teammate when_to_use: | You have a multi-agent team and need a coordinator that delegates work to teammates, monitors task status via TaskList/TaskGet, and synthesizes results. Lead roles require a team context — they have no value as standalone subagents. when_NOT_to_use: | Single-subagent workflows (a Task chain is simpler and cheaper). Work that does not require parallel delegation or real-time inter-agent communication. example_prompt_shape: | "You are the team lead. Delegate to via SendMessage and to . Monitor both with TaskList. When both complete, synthesize the results into a final report at ."

name: messenger purpose: minimal status relay between teammates; no reasoning, no file access typical_model: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 typical_effort: low typical_tools: [SendMessage] permission_mode: default isolation: team-teammate when_to_use: | You need a lightweight agent to ferry a status update, a signal, or a small payload between teammates. Messenger roles have no read tools and no write tools — they only relay messages. when_NOT_to_use: | Any task requiring file reads, file writes, or decisions. Use a lead or analyst role instead. example_prompt_shape: | "When this task completes, send 'done: ' to via SendMessage. Do nothing else."

name: adversarial-critic purpose: team-embedded adversarial reviewer; challenges proposals in real-time via SendMessage typical_model: claude-opus-4-7 typical_effort: xhigh typical_tools: [Read, Grep, Glob, SendMessage] permission_mode: default isolation: team-teammate effort_rationale: | Same rationale as the standalone critic: xhigh is the recommended starting point for Opus 4.7 deliberation work. In a team context, the adversarial-critic must evaluate multiple teammates' proposals concurrently, sustaining the need for deep deliberation. when_to_use: | You want continuous adversarial review inside a running agent team. The adversarial-critic receives proposals from other teammates via SendMessage and responds with specific objections before the team proceeds. when_NOT_to_use: | One-shot review after the fact (use the standalone critic — simpler, no team overhead). When team cost budget is tight (Opus xhigh in a team is expensive; consider critic at high on Sonnet 4.6). example_prompt_shape: | "When you receive a proposal via SendMessage, evaluate it for failure modes and false assumptions. Send your objections back to via SendMessage. Send only objections — do not send approval."
